rook-placement count spectrum

Primary locator: Lewis--Won, arXiv:2609.03081v1, definitions in Section 2, permutation grids in Section 3.2, and Conjecture 3.10.

An `m`-by-`n` crossword grid has white and black cells. An across word is a maximal contiguous white segment in one row; a down word is the analogous segment in one column. A nonattacking rook placement is a white-cell subset with at most one selected cell in each across and down word. It is complete when every across and every down word contains exactly one selected cell. `RP(G)` is the set of complete placements.

For `w in S_n`, `Grid(w)` has black cells `(i,w(i))`, one per row and column. Complete placements correspond to perfect matchings in the across-word/down-word incidence graph, and their count is the permanent of its biadjacency matrix.

Frozen assertion: the positive integers realized as `|RP(Grid(w))|`, over all `n>=1` and `w in S_n`, are exactly those other than `4`, `12`, and the integers congruent to `3 mod 4`.

Grid(w) is the n-by-n crossword grid whose black cells are (i,w(i)).
